matchups.recap: Nori got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by a football field and a half—53 points is the kind of margin you see when someone forgets to set their lineup entirely, except Nori apparently remembered to bench his entire offense. Rob put up 112 and still could've won by more if he'd started his kicker's grandmother. This wasn't a matchup, it was a mercy killing.

Ben got absolutely obliterated by a margin so massive it looks like a typo—67.5 fucking points. That's not a loss, that's a public execution; you scored 56.4 and got lapped like you're playing a different sport entirely. Your roster this week had all the firepower of a wet paper bag, and Arben just ran straight through it like he was bowling. Next time maybe actually set your lineup instead of whatever dumpster fire decision-making led to this catastrophe.

Veton got absolutely skull-fucked this week, limping across the finish line 18 points in the red like a one-legged horse at a glue factory. Flamur's squad showed up ready to play while Veton's roster looked like he drafted it during a blackout, fielding a collection of underperforming nobodies who couldn't score if the defense was asleep. The gap between these teams was so wide you could drive a fucking truck through it, and honestly Veton's probably still wondering what hit him—spoiler alert, it was his own incompetence.

Rinor got absolutely skull-fucked by a 45-point margin this week—that's not a loss, that's a goddamn public execution. Dude's roster looked like he drafted with his eyes closed and a concussion, while Faton was out here running a functional football team. At this point Rinor might as well check his lineups with a Magic 8-Ball because his decision-making has been shakier than a newborn giraffe all season.

Adam got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 20.6 points like he drafted his entire roster based on vibes and a fever dream. 74.6 points is what you score when your "late-round sleeper" turns out to be more of a comatose corpse, and your "bounce-back candidate" decides to bounce straight into the IR. Ilir walked into this matchup like he was playing your JV squad, and honestly, that's exactly what it looked like from the scoreboard.

Rilind got absolutely dicked down 97.2 to 87.2 this week—a straight-up 10-point beatdown that had more mercy than a mercy rule in Little League. At this point he's not just losing, he's losing *badly*, which is somehow worse than just being mediocre. Jetmir and Peter waltzed into the end zone while Rilind's lineup spent the afternoon looking like a practice squad. Better luck next week, chief—you're gonna need it.

matchups.preview: Two teams circling the drain at 2-4, but Ben's about to find out what rock bottom actually feels like—Rob's got just enough momentum this week to capitalize on whatever dumpster fire Ben's roster turns into. Ben's been drafting like he's playing checkers while everyone else plays chess, and this is the week his paper-thin depth chart finally implodes on national television.

Nori's cruising at 4-2 while Veton's out here looking like he drafted his entire roster blindfolded and hungover—the man's 0-6 and somehow still thinks he's got a shot. This week Veton's going to discover what it feels like to lose to someone who actually knows what a waiver wire is, and Nori's going to add another W to the column just by showing up.

Arben's rolling in at 5-1 like he accidentally stumbled into competence, but Faton's about to remind everyone why you don't get cute with your waiver wire pickups—this week Arben's luck dries up faster than his bench and Faton's scrappy ass squad is hungry to close that gap.

Muriqi's sitting pretty at 5-1, but let's be honest—that record's held together with duct tape and prayer, propped up by whatever waiver-wire lottery tickets actually hit. Asllani's nipping at your heels at 4-2, and this week you're about to find out what happens when your house of cards meets a team that's actually figured out how to string together competent weeks. Time to see if you're a legitimate contender or just a guy who got lucky enough to avoid the basement—spoiler alert: your playoff hopes are sweating.

Rinor's back to his usual 3-3 mediocrity—barely treading water while Jetmir and Peter are actually figuring out how to win games. This matchup is gonna be a bloodbath; Rinor's been held together with duct tape and prayer all season, and now he's gotta face a team that actually knows what the fuck they're doing. Better luck next week, buddy.

Adam's "2-4 record" is basically just a participation trophy at this point—dude's been treading water while Rilind's actively drowning at 1-5, which somehow makes this matchup a race to see who can fuck it up worse. Two teams held together with duct tape and prayer, but at least Adam can say he's only half-collapsed; Rilind's entire season is a dumpster fire that somehow keeps burning.
